note: One register per claim, all in one build. The replaced tests formed two members (CVIDs 100, 101) of one 2020 edition and handed `form_representations` a decision whose columns split that year; a build refuses two literals of one edition unless they are `co_delivered` (one member delivering both) or `case_aliases`, and sets every column window to the entry's shared window. So each claim moves to one of the two shapes a build reaches: the co-delivered member (STORE*, CODED, CLASSIFIED; `co_delivered` needs `column_metadata = "per_column"`), or the pooled pair whose only shared year is 2022 (TWICE, MIXED, PARTIAL, SIBLING, MISSING), where First's 2020-2021 and Second's 2023-2024 stay their own states. STORE*: the old parameters' types and lengths (text 200 / 18, decimal 53 / integer 0, unknown / integer 0), each column's own on its per-column alias window, one state, `unknown_data_type` only for the untyped column. CODED: the old coding cut inside the window becomes the edition cut 2020 / 2021 (SCB sets aside sub-year item validity), so the old single window spanning both states is two windows per column, each keeping its storage. TWICE: two entries with the same columns and window but their own evidence compose (the old duplicate case id) and the shared state names both. MIXED: one `shared` and one `per_column` entry over 2022 (the old mixed-mode pair) withhold the 2022 state and its windows. PARTIAL: entry 2 selects only Second's later edition, so its window is 2022-07..12; the old competing 2020-07..12 decision becomes this overlap, the only period withheld. SIBLING: Second's own definition and operational definition are not copied to (or from) the representative: the variable has no definition (conflicting_variable_fact) and the shared state neither (conflicting_representation_fact on the operational definition, the old test's two diagnostics); as in the old test, First's operational definition is blank and Second's 'Different interpretation', a dispute because the shared state never selects a donor. Second's source attribution (a regression leg beyond the old test) is the same dispute on the other column text. Neither disputed text reaches coverage as an unexplained_delivery_fact_change: the shared state nulls it and its conflicting_representation_fact explains that. MISSING: a `[[coding.omit]]` takes Second's state away, so 2022 lacks one member (missing_representation_metadata) and no state is manufactured. CLASSIFIED: a co-delivered member has one list for both literals, so the books agree and the shared state keeps the list and its book (the old agree case). No `unexplained_delivery_*` issue in any register is the old allowed `check_delivery_coverage` calls: each withheld or sibling-assigned window is explained. Window provenance stays null on every parallel window (the old `w.provenance is None`). Expected values are the replaced tests' asserted types, lengths, codes and diagnostics, with dates read off the fixture.
fails_if: store*: `form_representations` (source_representations.py) gives a per-column alias window the shared state's or its sibling's data type or length, or stops reporting unknown_data_type for the blank Datatyp; coded: per-column windows lose their storage when the shared state is cut; twice: equal entries are reported as conflicting, or the state keeps only one entry's attribution; mixed: entries that differ only in column_metadata compose; partial: a conflict withholds the whole shared window instead of its overlap (2022-01..06 disappears) or nothing; sibling: the shared state or the variable takes one sibling's definition, or the shared state takes Second's operational definition or source attribution; the coverage waiver (`_null_conflicting_facts`, source_formation.py) keeps the column's operational-definition or source-attribution claim on the window the shared state nulls (an unexplained_delivery_fact_change for Second 2022); missing: the slice with a missing member forms a state from the members present; classified: the shared state drops the agreed list or book; any register: a withheld or sibling-assigned window is no longer taken back from the coverage obligations (an unexplained_delivery_* issue), or a parallel window gets the entry's provenance
